A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEVEX, with matching methods, benchmarks, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, inference and exploration costs, component ablations, and cross-backbone prompt-transfer experiments in Tables 2–4 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds backbone comparisons, restricted-tool experiments, development-split sensitivity results, and a search trace.

M1.justification: The abstract-idea search tree, novelty-guided UCT, implementation loop, semantic backpropagation, expansion rules, and Appendix A prompts are unchanged. The restricted-tool variant is an experimental control; the proposed default procedure remains intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four BlindTest tasks and five BLINK tasks described in Section 4.1 and Appendix B. The added backbone, toolbox, and split experiments reuse this coverage without introducing different data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds Basic-tool SEVEX as an internal comparison variant against full-tool SEVEX and Naive. The existing Naive, SketchPad, SketchPad+APE, and search-component comparisons remain; Table 5 reuses the Naive and SketchPad comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 expands evaluation beyond v1's single-task cross-backbone transfer experiment with full-discovery comparisons across four BlindTest tasks using GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 4.0. It also introduces a restricted-tool control and two additional 30-image CircledLetter development splits, excluding their union from testing. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the original metrics and main search settings.

E4.justification: The original component ablations and qualitative analyses are retained. New Appendix C tests whether gains depend on external pretrained tools, examines sensitivity to development-set selection, and presents a per-trial search trace. These add substantive evidence about attribution, robustness, and search behavior.

E5.justification: v1 already reports Figure 5 averages over five independent runs. v2 additionally specifies five runs per new development split and reports means with within-split standard deviations in Table A2. This adds explicit variability reporting for one study without revising the original run counts.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–4 retain their values. Table 5 adds backbone/task results, including SEVEX averages of 62.4% for GPT-4o and 75.2% for Claude, while reusing Gemini and some LineIntersections entries. Table A1 adds a 73.3% basic-tool average versus 72.4% with full tools. Table A2 reports test accuracies of 88.00 ± 4.30% and 85.98 ± 3.86% under the new split protocol. These are additional results, not revised same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The search-tree definitions and priority equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. The added explanation of search behavior introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about automated task-wise discovery, semantic exploration, performance and efficiency, and model-specific prompting. The added experiments provide further support without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the toolbox ablation as evidence that external models are not the main source of BlindTest gains, while acknowledging task-specific benefits. It also acknowledges the Claude CircledLetter exception, explicitly limits split-stability conclusions to CircledLetter, and explains how initially weaker search nodes can support useful refinements.

D1.justification: Appendix C specifies the permitted and excluded tool functions and explains construction of the additional development splits and held-out test set. The original hyperparameters, tool descriptions, Appendix A prompts, and Appendix B development indices remain unchanged. No new code or data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 softens the research-gap description from lacking research to being underexplored and replaces the claim of the first agent-driven system with an agent-driven system. The same 25 cited works remain; bibliography corrections do not add related research.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 2.1, corrects grammar and terminology, and consistently identifies the CircledLetter ablation. It inserts a backbone subsection and an additional-analyses appendix, moves the existing Discussions appendix from C to D, and adds contact information and acknowledgements. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, Tables A1–A2, and Figure A1 using the established presentation style. Existing displays are retained, with localized resizing and relocation, corrected captions and the Figure 5 task label, and changes to reference-link coloring. The original figures and tables are not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation by extending the main multi-task comparisons beyond Gemini and adding a direct control for external-tool dependence, addressing important gaps in v1's evidence for generality and attribution. Table A2 adds repeated-run variability and development-split robustness evidence with an explicit CircledLetter-only limitation. These gains improve support for the central method while preserving the original experiments and technical material.
